These notes follow my code from transcript quantification (using Salmon) through differential gene expression and GO enrichment.

The analysis includes five freshly laid samples, five 36-hour normoxia samples, and five 36-hour hypoxia samples. The comparison extracted here is **hypoxia versus normoxia at 36 hours**.

## 1. Salmon transcript quantification on the HPC

Example script shown for **SRR18173236**.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Slurm resource requests: job name, nodes, tasks, time limit, and memory.
#SBATCH --job-name=ehjob
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=8
#SBATCH -t 4:00:00
#SBATCH --mem=8G

# Index-building command preserved from my script.
# Each line starts with #, so this block does NOT run during this submission.
# The FASTA contains the actual transcript and genome sequences.
# The decoy list identifies which sequences are genome decoys.
# Cmydas_index is the folder holding Salmon's searchable reference.
# salmon index \
#   -p 8 \
#   -d Chelonia_mydas.Decoys.txt \
#   -i Cmydas_index \
#   -t Chelonia.Txm_Gnm.fasta

# Quantify this sample using the existing index.
# -i: index folder
# -l A: automatically infer library type
# -r: input reads supplied as SINGLE-END data
# -p 8: use 8 threads
# -o: output folder for this sample
salmon quant -i Cmydas_index \
  -l A \
  -r /sciclone/home/emhamp/scr10/Biol504L/project/read_trim/Cmydas_embryo_SRR18173236.Fwd.20q.70nt.fastq.gz \
  -p 8 \
  -o Salmon_Quant/Cmydas_embryo_SRR18173236_Quant
```

The shown command processes one read file as single-end input.

```bash
# Run in the HPC project directory to submit the script to Slurm.
sbatch salmon_run.sh
```

Salmon writes `quant.sf` inside each sample's output folder. It estimates transcript abundance.

```bash
# Run in a LOCAL Mac terminal to copy results from the HPC.
# The local destination folder must already exist.
# Quotes protect the remote wildcard from the local shell.
scp -r 'emhamp@bora.sciclone.wm.edu:/sciclone/home/emhamp/scr10/Biol504L/project/Salmon_Quant/Cmydas*' ~/Desktop/Cmydas_Analysis/quant_data/
```
Turtle GTF and metadata were placed in `~/Desktop/Cmydas_DGE/`.

## 2. Load R packages



```{r}
# Install BiocManager only if it is missing.
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("BiocManager")

# Installation examples: uncomment only if a package is missing.
# BiocManager::install(c("tximport", "DESeq2", "apeglm", "txdbmaker",
#                       "AnnotationDbi", "AnnotationHub", "clusterProfiler",
#                       "enrichplot"))
# install.packages(c("readr", "ashr", "pheatmap", "tibble",
#                    "RColorBrewer", "dplyr", "ggplot2"))

library("tximport")       # Import Salmon estimates and summarize by gene
library("readr")          # Reading files into R
library("DESeq2")         # Differential gene expression and transformations
library("apeglm")         # Shrink fold changes for initial MA plots
library("ashr")           # Shrink fold changes for volcano plot and GO gene lists
library("txdbmaker")      # Read the GTF into a transcript database
library("AnnotationDbi")  # Query transcript/gene and functional annotations
library("pheatmap")       # Heatmaps
library("tibble")         # Convert row names into a gene column
library("RColorBrewer")   # Heatmap and bar-plot colors
library("dplyr")       # Filtering, mutate, case_when, and %>% (organizing results)
library("ggplot2")        # Volcano plot and plot formatting
library("AnnotationHub")  # Retrieve the turtle annotation database
library("clusterProfiler") # GO enrichment
library("enrichplot")     # Enrichment visualizations
```

## 3. Make the transcript-to-gene table

```{r}
# Folder containing the GTF, metadata, and saved R results.
dir <- "/Users/emilyhamp/Desktop/Cmydas_DGE/"

# Read the turtle GTF annotation into a transcript database.
txdb <- makeTxDbFromGFF(
  file = file.path(dir, "GCF_015237465.2_rCheMyd1.pri.v2_genomic.gtf"),
  format = "gtf"
)

# Extract transcript names from the annotation.
k <- keys(txdb, keytype = "TXNAME")

# Find the gene corresponding to each transcript.
# Multiple transcripts can belong to the same gene.
tx2gene <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  txdb,
  keys = k,
  columns = "GENEID",
  keytype = "TXNAME"
)

head(tx2gene) # Inspect the first few transcript-to-gene pairs

# Save the table we just created; this is not a separate downloaded input.
write.csv(
  tx2gene,
  file = file.path(dir, "Cmydas.tx2gene.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

The GTF mapping needs to match the transcript identifiers in the Salmon reference.

## 4. Read metadata and locate the Salmon files

```{r}
# Read the metadata CSV into an R data frame called samples.
samples <- read.csv(file.path(dir, "Sea_Turtle_Metadata.csv"))
head(samples)

# Salmon results are in a separate folder from the GTF and metadata.
quant_dir <- "/Users/emilyhamp/Desktop/Cmydas_Analysis/quant_data"

# Remove spaces before/after the sequencing-run IDs.
samples$SRRs <- trimws(samples$SRRs)

# Construct folder names such as Cmydas_embryo_SRR18173250_Quant.
samples$quant_folder <- paste0(
  "Cmydas_embryo_",
  samples$SRRs,
  "_Quant"
)

# Construct one complete quant.sf path per metadata row.
quant_files <- file.path(quant_dir, samples$quant_folder, "quant.sf")

# Label the paths and metadata rows with the same sample identifiers.
# This labels their existing order; it does not sort the samples.
names(quant_files) <- samples$SRRs
rownames(samples) <- samples$SRRs

head(quant_files)
file.exists(quant_files) # Should print TRUE for every sample
stopifnot(all(file.exists(quant_files))) # Stop if any file is missing

# Import Salmon estimates and combine transcripts belonging to the same gene.
# tximport also retains abundance/length information used by the DESeq2 import.
txi <- tximport(quant_files, type = "salmon", tx2gene = tx2gene)
```

## 5. Define groups and create the DESeq2 dataset

```{r}
# Use the Condition text in the metadata to assign experimental groups.
# In this specific metadata file, the remaining samples are freshly laid.
# For another dataset, check unmatched conditions rather than assuming this.
samples$group <- factor(
  ifelse(
    grepl("normoxia", samples$Condition, ignore.case = TRUE),
    "Normoxia",
    ifelse(
      grepl("hypoxia", samples$Condition, ignore.case = TRUE),
      "Hypoxia",
      "Freshly_laid"
    )
  ),
  levels = c("Normoxia", "Hypoxia", "Freshly_laid")
)

table(samples$group) # Expected from my metadata: 5 samples per group

# Build the dataset from gene-level Salmon imports and sample metadata.
# ~ group models differences among the three groups.
# Normoxia is the reference because it is the first factor level.
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromTximport(
  txi,
  colData = samples,
  design = ~ group
)

# Genes are rows; samples are columns; entries are count estimates.
View(counts(dds))
```

## 6. Explore sample relationships

```{r}
# Transform counts for PCA and heatmaps. Prepare the values without using the treatment-group labels. 
rld = rlog(dds, blind = TRUE)

# PCA summarizes major expression patterns; points are colored by group.
plotPCA(rld, intgroup = "group")

# Create group labels for the sample-correlation heatmap.
meta <- data.frame(
  group = samples$group,
  row.names = colnames(dds)
)

rld_mat <- assay(rld)     # Extract the transformed expression matrix
rld_corr <- cor(rld_mat)  # Calculate correlations between sample columns

# Plot how similar samples are to one another.
pheatmap(rld_corr, annotation = meta)
```


## 7. Filter low counts and run differential expression

```{r}
# Keep genes with at least 10 counts TOTAL across all samples.
# This does not require 10 counts in each individual sample.
good_rows <- rowSums(counts(dds)) >= 10
dds <- dds[good_rows,]

# Fit the DESeq2 model, accounting for normalization and count variation.
dds <- DESeq(dds)

resultsNames(dds) # Display the fitted model's coefficient names

# Extract Hypoxia relative to Normoxia at 36 hours.
# Positive log2 fold change = higher estimated expression in hypoxia.
# Negative log2 fold change = lower estimated expression in hypoxia.
res_hypoxia_normoxia <- results(
  dds,
  contrast = c("group", "Hypoxia", "Normoxia"),
  alpha = 0.05
)

summary(res_hypoxia_normoxia)
```

`log2FoldChange` reports the effect size. `padj` reports the multiple-testing-adjusted p-value. A log2 fold change of 1 corresponds to a twofold ratio.

## 8. Shrink fold changes with apeglm and make MA plots

```{r}
# Shrink uncertain log2 fold-change estimates using apeglm.
res_hypoxia_normoxia_apeglm <- lfcShrink(
  dds,
  coef = "group_Hypoxia_vs_Normoxia",
  type = "apeglm",
  res = res_hypoxia_normoxia
)

summary(res_hypoxia_normoxia_apeglm)

# MA plots: mean normalized expression versus log2 fold change.
# Compare the original and shrunken estimates.
plotMA(res_hypoxia_normoxia, ylim = c(-2, 2))
plotMA(res_hypoxia_normoxia_apeglm, ylim = c(-2, 2))

# Save the apeglm results.
out_csv <- file.path(dir, "Hypoxia_vs_Normoxia.DEG.csv")
write.csv(as.data.frame(res_hypoxia_normoxia_apeglm), file = out_csv)
```

## 9. Follow-up shrinkage with ashr

I followed the class's second shrinkage example. The subsequent volcano plot and GO gene sets use the ashr estimates.

```{r}
# Explicitly set Normoxia as reference (it was already the reference above).
dds$group <- relevel(dds$group, ref = "Normoxia")
dds <- DESeq(dds)

result_hypoxia_normoxia_ashr <- lfcShrink(
  dds,
  contrast = c("group", "Hypoxia", "Normoxia"),
  type = "ashr",
  alpha = 0.05
)

summary(result_hypoxia_normoxia_ashr)

# Use the sequencing-run IDs as the sample column labels.
samples$sample_name <- samples$SRRs
colnames(dds) <- samples$sample_name
```

## 10. Make the normalized-count heatmap

```{r}
# Extract normalized counts and store gene identifiers in a column.
normalized_counts <- data.frame(counts(dds, normalized = TRUE))
normalized_counts <- tibble::rownames_to_column(
  normalized_counts,
  var = "gene"
)

# Choose a reversed red/yellow/blue color palette.
heat_colors <- rev(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(6, "RdYlBu"))

# Exclude column 1 (gene names), leaving all 15 sample columns.
pheatmap(as.matrix(normalized_counts[, -1]),
         color = heat_colors,
         cluster_rows = TRUE,  # Group genes with similar patterns
         cluster_cols = TRUE,  # Group samples with similar patterns
         show_rownames = FALSE, # Hide thousands of gene labels
         border_color = NA,
         fontsize = 10,
         scale = "row",        # Show relative values within each gene
         treeheight_row = 0,    # Hide the gene dendrogram
         height = 20)
```


## 11. Label expression changes and make the volcano plot

```{r}
# Convert ashr results to a data frame and preserve the gene IDs.
res_df <- as.data.frame(result_hypoxia_normoxia_ashr)
res_df <- tibble::rownames_to_column(res_df, var = "gene")

# Remove genes lacking an adjusted p-value from this plotting/enrichment table.
res_df <- res_df %>% filter(!is.na(padj))

# Label genes using BOTH an effect-size and a significance threshold.
# UP: more than twofold higher estimated expression in hypoxia.
# DOWN: less than half the estimated expression in hypoxia.
# NOT: does not meet both criteria; it does not prove no biological effect.
res_df <- res_df %>%
  mutate(diffexpressed = case_when(
    log2FoldChange > 1 & padj < 0.05 ~ "UP",
    log2FoldChange < -1 & padj < 0.05 ~ "DOWN",
    TRUE ~ "NOT"
  ))

table(res_df$diffexpressed) # Count genes assigned to each label

# Plot effect size against statistical evidence, with one point per gene.
ggplot(res_df, aes(
  x = log2FoldChange,
  y = -log10(padj),
  color = diffexpressed
)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("DOWN" = "blue", "NOT" = "grey", "UP" = "red")
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "log2 Fold Change (Hypoxia / Normoxia)",
    y = "-log10 Adjusted p-value",
    color = "Expression"
  )
```


## 12. Find the turtle GO annotation database

```{r}
ah <- AnnotationHub()

# Search for a turtle organism annotation database.
turtle_annotations <- query(ah, c("Chelonia mydas", "OrgDb"))
turtle_annotations

# The search returned this turtle record; load it.
org_db <- ah[["AH120704"]]

# Check supported identifier types and available annotations.
AnnotationDbi::keytypes(org_db)
AnnotationDbi::columns(org_db)

# Check how many result gene names match database gene symbols.
symbol_matches <- res_df$gene %in%
  AnnotationDbi::keys(org_db, keytype = "SYMBOL")

table(symbol_matches)
```

My output showed **17,679 symbol matches and 369 nonmatches**, using the returned AnnotationHub snapshot of 2026-04-23. 

## 13. Prepare gene sets and run GO enrichment

```{r}
# Separate all selected DEGs, UP genes, and DOWN genes.
sig_degs <- res_df %>% filter(diffexpressed != "NOT")
only_up_degs <- res_df %>% filter(diffexpressed == "UP")
only_down_degs <- res_df %>% filter(diffexpressed == "DOWN")

# Extract the gene names rather than the entire result rows.
all_gene_names <- res_df$gene
sig_deg_names <- sig_degs$gene
sig_up_names <- only_up_degs$gene
sig_down_names <- only_down_degs$gene

clean_sig_deg_names <- sig_deg_names
clean_uni_names <- all_gene_names
clean_sig_up_names <- sig_up_names
clean_sig_down_names <- sig_down_names

# Combined UP and DOWN gene set: biological-process enrichment.
ego <- enrichGO(
  gene = clean_sig_deg_names,
  universe = clean_uni_names, # Background: genes in my processed res_df
  OrgDb = org_db,             # Turtle annotations
  keyType = "SYMBOL",         # Identifier type used by my result genes
  ont = "BP",                 # Biological process
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",       # Benjamini-Hochberg multiple-testing adjustment
  qvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  readable = TRUE
)

# UP genes: test all three GO categories for the faceted plot.
sig_up_ego <- enrichGO(
  gene = clean_sig_up_names,
  universe = clean_uni_names,
  OrgDb = org_db,
  keyType = "SYMBOL",
  ont = "ALL",                # BP, molecular function, cellular component
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  qvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  readable = TRUE
)

# DOWN genes: biological-process enrichment.
sig_down_ego <- enrichGO(
  gene = clean_sig_down_names,
  universe = clean_uni_names,
  OrgDb = org_db,
  keyType = "SYMBOL",
  ont = "BP",
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  qvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  readable = TRUE
)
```

GO enrichment tests whether annotated functions occur more often in a selected gene set than expected from the background. 

## 14. Visualize and save GO enrichment

```{r}
# Display up to 50 enriched terms for each gene set.
dotplot(ego, showCategory = 50)
dotplot(sig_up_ego, showCategory = 50)
dotplot(sig_down_ego, showCategory = 50)

# Convert results into ordinary tables for viewing and saving.
goa_summary <- data.frame(ego)
up_goa_summary <- data.frame(sig_up_ego)
down_goa_summary <- data.frame(sig_down_ego)

write.csv(
  goa_summary,
  file.path(dir, "Hypoxia_vs_Normoxia.All_DEGs.GOEnrichment.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
write.csv(
  up_goa_summary,
  file.path(dir, "Hypoxia_vs_Normoxia.UpReg_DEGs.GOEnrichment.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
write.csv(
  down_goa_summary, # Use the DOWN table, not a duplicate of the UP table
  file.path(dir, "Hypoxia_vs_Normoxia.DownReg_DEGs.GOEnrichment.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Connect similar GO terms; default similarity uses shared genes.
# This is a network of TERMS, not physical interactions between genes.
ego_sim <- enrichplot::pairwise_termsim(ego)
enrichplot::emapplot(ego_sim, showCategory = 50)

head(up_goa_summary)
head(down_goa_summary)

# Show UP enrichment as bars, split into the three GO categories.
# Bar length is the associated gene count, not fold-change magnitude.
p_facet <- barplot(
  sig_up_ego,
  x = "Count",
  showCategory = 15,
  split = "ONTOLOGY"
) +
  aes(fill = ONTOLOGY) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  enrichplot::autofacet(by = "row", scales = "free")

p_facet + scale_y_discrete()
```
## What my GO enrichment analysis compared

My GO enrichment analysis compared the functions represented in my selected genes with the functions represented in the background genes from my analysis.

- **Selected genes:** my UP genes, DOWN genes, or both combined. These genes had an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change greater than 1.
- **Background genes:** all genes remaining in `res_df`, including UP, DOWN, and NOT genes. Genes without usable GO annotations could not contribute to the relevant enrichment comparison.

The turtle annotation database supplied information about which functions each gene is associated with. It was not a separate control expression dataset.

For example, if 10% of the annotated background genes were associated with oxygen transport, but 40% of my UP genes were associated with it, GO enrichment would test whether this function was unusually common among my UP genes. 

DESeq2 compared expression between **hypoxia and normoxia samples**. GO enrichment then compared the functions represented in my **selected gene sets** with those represented in my **background gene set**.

## 15. Save the processed results and dataset

```{r}
# Save the ashr results used downstream, including gene IDs and labels.
write.csv(
  res_df,
  file.path(dir, "Hypoxia_vs_Normoxia.ashr.DGE.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Save normalized gene counts for all samples.
write.csv(
  normalized_counts,
  file.path(dir, "Cmydas.NormalizedCounts.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Save the fitted DESeq2 dataset.
save(dds, file = file.path(dir, "Cmydas.DDS.rda"))
```

These commands save files in `Cmydas_DGE`; they do not open a new plot or table. Figures must be exported separately. The biological interpretation still requires examining the actual gene lists, adjusted p-values, sample patterns, and enriched terms.


## Short methods summary

RNA-seq transcript abundances were quantified with Salmon on the HPC and imported into R with tximport using a transcript-to-gene mapping derived from the *C. mydas* rCheMyd1.pri.v2 GTF annotation. Fifteen samples were assigned to freshly laid, 36-hour normoxia, and 36-hour hypoxia groups, with five samples per group. Sample relationships were explored using rlog-transformed PCA and correlation heatmaps. Genes with fewer than 10 total counts across samples were removed, and DESeq2 was fitted with `design = ~ group`. Hypoxia was contrasted against normoxia. Both apeglm and ashr fold-change shrinkage were explored; downstream gene classification used ashr estimates, adjusted p-value < 0.05, and absolute log2 fold change > 1. GO overrepresentation analysis used clusterProfiler and the turtle AnnotationHub OrgDb record AH120704 with gene symbols and the analyzed, non-missing-padj gene set as the supplied background. Combined and DOWN gene sets were tested for biological-process enrichment, while the UP set was tested across all three GO categories. Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment and a q-value cutoff of 0.05 were specified.
